title: Planetarium view hotkeys swallow typing in the search field - object search by name is unusable from the keyboard
what_happened: With the planetarium plan panel open and the caret blinking in the 'Search objects, names...' field, typing 'Vega' deterministically leaves 'Va' in the field: the 'e' toggled the ecliptic layer on and the 'g' toggled the equatorial grid on instead of entering text. Typing the full lowercase alphabet 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left only 'abd' in the field - c/e/f/g/h/m/n/r are all bound to view actions (constellation lines, ecliptic, FOV overlay, grid, reset view, minimap, now) and after 'h' (reset view) the field lost focus entirely so i..z were dropped too. Reproduced at 30ms, 250ms, 400ms and 2000ms inter-key delays: it is a shortcut conflict, not a dropped-keystroke race.
expected: A focused text field must consume ordinary character keys. Planetarium single-letter hotkeys should be suppressed whenever the primary focus is a text input (Flutter: check FocusManager.instance.primaryFocus?.context?.widget is EditableText, or move the shortcuts into a Shortcuts/Actions scope that a TextField's own shortcut scope shadows).
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > click the sidebar toggle (top right) > click the 'Search objects, names...' field > type Vega. Field shows 'Va'; the ecliptic line and the RA/Dec grid have both switched on behind the panel.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-11.png (grid + ecliptic appeared while typing 'Vega'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-18.png ('Va' after 400ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-19.png ('Va' after 2000ms/char), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-20.png ('abd' after typing the whole alphabet). Handler: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/planetarium_screen/actions.dart:507-624
proposed_fix: In _handleKeyEvent, return KeyEventResult.ignored early when the primary focus is an editable text field, before the single-letter branches.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim on a fresh v-planetarium profile (site 40.00N/105.00W). Plan Tonight > Planetarium > sidebar toggle > click 'Search objects, names...' > type 'Vega' left literally 'Va' in the field, and the RA/Dec grid (labels +30/+15/0/-15, 3h..23h) plus the yellow ecliptic line both switched on behind the panel (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vp-09.png before, vp-10.png after). Clearing and typing 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' left exactly 'abd' (vp-12.png) - character for character what was reported. The focus-loss half of the claim also reproduced: after the alphabet run the field no longer had focus, and later keystrokes went to the sky (a stray 'h'/'r' recentred the view on the zenith, RA 5h48m = LST, Dec +40 = latitude). Code confirms the mechanism: planetarium_screen.dart:259-262 wraps the whole screen in Focus(autofocus:true, onKeyEvent:_handleKeyEvent), and _handleKeyEvent (actions.dart:507) returns KeyEventResult.handled for bare keyH/keyR/keyG/keyC/keyE/keyN/keyM/keyF with no test for whether primaryFocus is a text input, so the ancestor Focus eats KeyEvents that the TextField's IME text path never sees. Severity P1 is right: naming a target is the primary way into this screen and it cannot be typed. Cited location actions.dart:551-600 does contain the single-letter branches; the guard belongs at the top of _handleKeyEvent (actions.dart:507).

title: At a 1-degree imaging FOV the sky renders essentially empty - measured 1 star in 0.6 sq deg at astronomical dark
what_happened: Zoomed to the minimum FOV (1.0 deg short axis), time set to tonight's astro dark via the TONIGHT button, view at the zenith (RA 17h44m, Dec +40, in Hercules): an 800x400 px patch of sky - 0.59 sq deg - contained ONE barely-visible dot (2 local maxima above grey level 40, zero above 60, on a background of 12). Star counts measured in the same pixel window while zooming out at the same sky centre: FOV 1.0 -> 1 star, 2.0 -> 6, 4.1 -> 33, 8.1 -> 74, 16.4 -> 328. Sky area scales as FOV^2, so surface density is flat at 1.7-3.5 stars/sq deg at every zoom - i.e. the depth never increases as you zoom in, and 2.9 stars/sq deg is exactly the whole bundled HYG catalog (119,600 stars over 41,253 sq deg), which is complete only to about mag 9.
expected: An imaging-scale field is the whole point of a planetarium inside an astrophotography app - it is what you check framing and guide stars against. At 1 deg it should show tens of stars. The bundled catalog is the binding constraint, not the FOV-adaptive magnitude ramp, which the code intends to add up to +7 mag by 1 deg.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > wheel-zoom to FOV 1.0 deg > press TONIGHT in the time bar > look at the sky.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fov1-night2.png (the empty 800x400 field), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/fovzoom-2.png .. fovzoom-16.png (counts above). Bundled catalog: apps/desktop/.../assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1/tiles = 3,458,592 bytes over 768 tiles, ~28.7 bytes/star -> ~119,600 stars = full HYG.
location_wrong: render_config.dart:434-489 does contain the FOV magnitude ramp, but that code is not the defect and editing it changes nothing on screen - at FOV 1.2 at astro dark it already reaches its 12.0 clamp, and the shipped pack has zero stars between mag 9.0 and 12.0 anywhere in this field. The finding's own 'expected' says the catalog is the binding constraint, yet the where still points at the ramp. Actionable sites: the bundled pack depth (apps/desktop/assets/planetarium/catalogs/stars-hyg-v1 + build_hyg_tiles), the deep-star tier (deep_star_providers.dart - showDeepStarsProvider default false, kDeepStarFovThresholdDegrees 8.0, kHygFaintFloorMag 11.5; layers_panel.dart:413-460; deep_star_catalog_card.dart:250 which asks the user for their own self-hosted base URL because no tileset is published), and the missing signal (star_catalog_fallback_banner.dart fires only when HYG is absent entirely, never when HYG's mag-9 floor is what is emptying the field).
proposed_fix: Ship (or auto-fetch on first run) a Tycho-2-depth tileset, and set the HYG hand-off seam to HYG's real completeness (~9.0), not 11.5.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced and the cause proved from the shipped catalog binary rather than from the app. TONIGHT set the clock to 2026-08-03 00:00 (astro dusk); scroll-zoomed to FOV 1.2 deg short axis centred on M57 (RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d01'). The sky canvas covers 2.271 x 1.200 deg = 2.725 sq deg and contained 12 star blobs by an 8-connected >=3px detector on the raw capture (vp-24.png, vp-25.png) = 4.4 stars/sq deg. I then decoded the bundled pack myself: 768 NSPLNT01 tiles, 64-byte header + 16*lod_levels LOD index + 28-byte records {u32 id, u32 flags, f32 x,y,z unit vector, f32 mag, f32 B-V}; layout validated by recovering HIP 14135 = Menkar at RA 3h02m, Dec +4.09, mag 2.54. Total 119,432 stars = 2.90/sq deg whole sky, saturating at mag ~10 (N<=9 = 83,479; N<=12 = 117,930; N<=15 = 119,432), i.e. complete only to about mag 9 exactly as claimed. In the exact rendered footprint the pack holds 13 stars, faintest mag 9.0, with nothing fainter than 9.0 present at all. So the app draws 12 of the 13 stars it owns - the renderer is not dropping anything, the catalog is empty. A real Lyra field (b ~ +13) carries of order 100-200 stars/sq deg to mag 12, so the chart is ~30x too shallow at imaging scale, and layers_panel.dart:415-419 documents that no deep tileset is published, making mag ~9 a hard ceiling for a shipped user. One number needs correcting downward: the headline '1 star in 0.6 sq deg' is an unlucky patch - the honest density is ~3-5 stars/sq deg (2.90 whole-sky pack mean, 4.4 measured), so '1 star' overstates the emptiness by a factor of a few. P1 stands: framing and guide-star checks at imaging scale are a headline use of this screen.

title: Object info popup keeps the old object's name and coordinates but recomputes Alt/Az for the NEW selection - it said Deneb was 'Below Horizon' while Deneb was 11.5 deg up
what_happened: Clicked the star Deneb on the chart; the popup opened correctly (Deneb / HIP102098 / mag 1.3 / Star (A2Ia) / RA 20h 41m 25.9s / Dec +45d 16' 49" / Current Position 12.2 deg, Az 320.1 deg, badge 'Daylight'). Without closing it, I selected M57 from the search results. The view recentred on M57 (Center RA 18h53m35s, Dec +33d 01') and the selection ring moved, but the popup stayed open still headed 'Deneb' with Deneb's identifier, magnitude, spectral type and RA/Dec - while its 'Current Position' block changed to '-10.3 deg, Az 331.2 deg' with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. Independent computation for that instant (2026-08-02 14:51:01 UTC, 40N 105W): Deneb is at alt +11.46 deg, az 320.93 deg; M57 is at alt -10.33 deg, az 331.20 deg. The popup is therefore showing M57's horizon position under Deneb's name, to the 0.1 deg. It is not a one-frame race: 74 seconds later it still read Deneb / -10.4 deg / Az 331.4 deg, which again tracks M57 (-10.4 / 331.4) and not Deneb (+11.4 / 321.0). The popup also carries a 'Slew' button, so the object the user is reading about and the object the app considers selected are not the same thing at the moment they press it.
expected: The popup must either follow the new selection wholesale or close. Half-following - identity and catalogue coordinates from object A, live altitude/azimuth and the 'Below Horizon' warning from object B - is the worst of the three, because the visible result is a true-looking sentence about the wrong star.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium. Click a bright star (Deneb) to open its info popup. Leave it open. In the right panel's Search tab type '6720' and click the M57 result. The popup still says Deneb but its Current Position row now reports M57's altitude and azimuth and flags 'Below Horizon'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (popup for Deneb: Alt 12.2, Az 320.1, 'Daylight'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-33.png (after selecting M57: view centred at RA 18h53m35s Dec +33 01', popup still headed Deneb, Alt -10.3 Az 331.2 'Below Horizon'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-34.png (74 s later: Deneb, -10.4, Az 331.4, still 'Below Horizon'). Computed truth at 14:51:01 UTC from 40N/105W: Deneb +11.46/320.93, M57 -10.33/331.20.
location_wrong: Symptom and file are right, but the finding omits the second half of the defect: the stale value lives in the SHELL, not the popup. object_info_popup.dart:476 (`final altAz = ref.watch(selectedObjectAltAzProvider)!`) is the read site; the field that goes stale is `_popupObject` (planetarium_screen.dart:101), written only on a sky tap (actions.dart:100-103), cleared in _dismissPopup (actions.dart:110-116) and passed to the popup at widgets/redesign/planetarium_shell.dart:303-306. A fixer who only touches object_info_popup.dart can make alt/az agree with the header while still leaving a popup describing an object that is no longer selected. One sub-claim is wrong: the finding says the Slew button targets a different object than the popup describes. It does not - _handleSlewToTarget, _sendToFraming, _addToSequencer and _addPopupObjectToTargetQueue all read `_popupObject` (actions.dart:141, 243, 266, 320, 327), so every action button acts on the object NAMED in the popup. Only the Current Position row and the observability badge come from the other object.
proposed_fix: Bind the whole popup to one immutable object snapshot taken when it opens (and dismiss/replace it on selection change), instead of reading identity from a captured object and the live horizon block from selectedObjectProvider.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a different object pair and checked against my own alt/az code, not the app's. Clicked a star on the chart: popup opened for HIP24951 (mag 6.5, A2V+, RA 5h20m39.2s, Dec +46d57'49"), Current Position 81.2 deg / Az 325.0 deg, badge 'Daylight' (vp-15.png). Without closing it I typed '6720' in the panel search and clicked the M57 result (vp-16.png, 2026-08-02 16:05:25 UTC): view recentred on RA 18h53m35s Dec +33d01', selection ring moved to M57, popup still read HIP24951 with all of HIP24951's catalogue data, but Current Position flipped to -15.5 deg / Az 346.2 deg with a red 'Below Horizon' badge. My independent GMST/LST spherical transform for that instant at 40N/105W: HIP24951 alt +81.19 az 324.67; M57 alt -15.54 az 346.31 (LST 5h50.5m vs the app footer's 05:50). Then a second instant in the opposite direction: pressing TONIGHT moved the clock to 2026-08-03 00:00:03 local (04:00:03 UTC) and the same stale popup, still headed HIP24951, showed Alt 75.0 / Az 112.4 with a GREEN 'Excellent' badge (vp-17.png) - computed truth M57 75.0/112.4, HIP24951 -2.8/4.5. So the app badged a star 2.8 deg below the horizon as an excellent target. Matching the other object to 0.1 deg in both directions, and surviving a time change, rules out any one-frame race.
